title: Automotive Basics
description: Build confidence with engines, maintenance, brakes, steering and diagnosis.

lessons.title: Understand the system
lessons.body: Identify what each component does before diagnosing a fault. A symptom or trouble code is a starting point, not proof that a particular part has failed.

lessons.title: Use vehicle-specific information
lessons.body: Follow the service manual for fluids, lifting points, torque values and procedures. Stop driving with serious braking, steering or oil-pressure problems.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of engine oil?
questions.explanation: Oil reduces friction between moving engine parts.

questions.question: Which component stores electrical energy for starting a conventional vehicle?
questions.explanation: The battery supplies electrical energy when the engine is not running.

questions.question: What does an alternator do while the engine is running?
questions.explanation: The alternator supplies electrical power and charges the battery.

questions.question: What does the radiator primarily help remove?
questions.explanation: The radiator transfers coolant heat to surrounding air.

questions.question: What does an engine thermostat regulate?
questions.explanation: The thermostat controls coolant flow as engine temperature changes.

questions.question: In a gasoline engine, what normally ignites the compressed mixture?
questions.explanation: A spark initiates combustion in a spark-ignition engine.

questions.question: How does a conventional diesel engine ignite its fuel?
questions.explanation: Compression heats the air enough for injected diesel fuel to ignite.

questions.question: What does an intake air filter do?
questions.explanation: Filtering incoming air helps protect engine components.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a fuel injector?
questions.explanation: An injector delivers controlled amounts of fuel.

questions.question: Which system carries combustion gases away from the engine?
questions.explanation: Exhaust passages carry gases away from the cylinders.

questions.question: What does a catalytic converter help do?
questions.explanation: Catalysts help convert certain pollutants into less harmful substances.

questions.question: What does a differential allow during a turn?
options: All tires to rotate at identical speeds
Driven wheels to rotate at different speeds
Brake fluid to bypass the master cylinder
questions.explanation: The outer wheel travels farther during a turn and needs a different speed.

questions.question: What does a conventional manual-transmission clutch do?
options: Connect or disconnect engine power from the gearbox
questions.explanation: The clutch allows power transfer to be interrupted for starting and shifting.

questions.question: Which part do disc-brake pads press against?
questions.explanation: Pads create friction against the rotor to slow the wheel.

questions.question: Which part do drum-brake shoes press against?
questions.explanation: Brake shoes press outward against the drum.

questions.question: What is ABS designed to help prevent during hard braking?
questions.explanation: ABS modulates braking to reduce wheel lockup; traction limits still apply.

questions.question: Where should you find the recommended cold tire pressure for a passenger car?
questions.explanation: Use the vehicle recommendation rather than treating the tire's maximum as the target.

questions.question: What does tire tread help channel away on wet pavement?
questions.explanation: Tread grooves help manage water; worn tires reduce wet traction.

questions.question: What is a shock absorber mainly designed to control?
questions.explanation: Dampers control spring movement and help maintain tire contact.

questions.question: What does a ball joint allow in a suspension?
options: Fuel to flow into the tank
questions.explanation: A ball joint accommodates movement between suspension components.

questions.question: What do tie rods connect in a typical steering system?
options: Steering linkage to the wheel steering arms
questions.explanation: Tie rods transmit steering movement to the wheels.

questions.question: What is the best response to a sudden loss of braking effectiveness?
options: Keep driving until the next oil change
Add engine oil to the brake reservoir
Stop safely and arrange qualified inspection
questions.explanation: A braking problem requires prompt evaluation before continued driving.

questions.question: What does an OBD-II trouble code usually provide?
options: Proof that one named part must be replaced
questions.explanation: Codes identify detected conditions; testing is still needed to determine the cause.

questions.question: What is an engine misfire?
options: A change in wheel bolt pattern
Incomplete or missing combustion in a cylinder
questions.explanation: Misfires can have ignition, fuel, compression or other causes.

questions.question: What should you do with a flashing check-engine light and rough running?
options: Reduce load, stop safely and consult service guidance
Drive harder to clear the fault
Ignore it if the radio works
questions.explanation: Flashing warnings can indicate damaging misfires; avoid continued operation and seek guidance.

questions.question: When should you remove a pressurized radiator cap?
options: With the engine at full throttle
Only when safe and cool as directed by the manual
questions.explanation: Hot pressurized coolant can cause severe burns.

questions.question: Why check fluid specifications before topping up?
options: Any oil works in any system
All fluids use the same formula
questions.explanation: The required specification matters more than appearance.

questions.question: What does a serpentine belt commonly drive?
questions.explanation: Accessory layouts vary, so inspect the specific vehicle's belt routing.

questions.question: What should you do if an accessory belt is badly frayed?
options: Arrange replacement and inspect related components
Cut off loose sections and keep driving
questions.explanation: Fraying indicates damage; tensioners and pulleys may also need inspection.

questions.question: What is a wheel bearing's main role?
options: Support wheel rotation with low friction
questions.explanation: Wheel bearings support rotating wheel loads.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a CV joint?
options: Transmit torque while accommodating angle changes
questions.explanation: CV joints allow drive axles to transmit power through changing angles.

questions.question: Why inspect a torn CV boot promptly?
options: It makes the fuel tank leak
It can let lubricant out and contamination in
It automatically proves the axle is bent
questions.explanation: The boot protects the lubricated joint from dirt and moisture.

questions.question: What does the master cylinder do in a hydraulic brake system?
options: Convert pedal input into hydraulic pressure
questions.explanation: The master cylinder pressurizes brake fluid when the pedal is applied.

questions.question: What is a brake-fluid leak a reason to do?
options: Top up repeatedly and ignore it
Stop using the vehicle and arrange repair
questions.explanation: Leaks can cause loss of braking and require proper repair.

questions.question: What does a parking brake primarily do?
questions.explanation: Use it according to the manual, together with correct parking procedures.

questions.question: What does engine compression describe?
options: Pressure developed as the piston compresses cylinder contents
questions.explanation: Compression testing can help assess cylinder sealing.

questions.question: What is a cylinder leak-down test used to investigate?
questions.explanation: Leak-down testing can help locate sealing losses through valves, rings or other paths.

questions.question: Why record symptoms before starting a repair?
options: They help reproduce and narrow the fault
questions.explanation: Operating conditions and symptom patterns guide useful testing.

questions.question: Why compare a replacement belt with the correct application data?
options: Length and routing must suit the vehicle
questions.explanation: Correct application data prevents incorrect belt selection.

questions.question: What does a cabin air filter commonly filter?
options: Air entering the passenger ventilation system
questions.explanation: Cabin filters reduce particles in ventilation air.

questions.question: Which part transfers piston motion to the crankshaft?
questions.explanation: The connecting rod links the piston to the crankshaft.

questions.question: What does the camshaft control in a conventional four-stroke engine?
questions.explanation: Cam lobes operate the valve mechanism at the required timing.

questions.question: What are the four strokes of a conventional four-stroke engine?
questions.explanation: The cycle takes two crankshaft revolutions.

questions.question: What does a turbocharger use to drive its turbine?
questions.explanation: Exhaust flow drives a turbine coupled to the intake compressor.

questions.question: What does an intercooler do in many turbocharged systems?
questions.explanation: Cooling compressed air reduces its temperature before entering the engine.

questions.question: Why follow the specified wheel-fastener torque?
options: All wheels use one universal value
Correct clamping is needed without overstressing fasteners
questions.explanation: Use the specified torque, sequence and tool rather than guessing.

questions.question: What does wheel alignment concern?
options: Wheel angles relative to specified geometry
questions.explanation: Alignment affects tracking, handling and tire wear.

questions.question: What does wheel balancing correct?
options: Uneven mass distribution in a rotating wheel assembly
questions.explanation: Balancing reduces vibration caused by uneven rotating mass.

questions.question: What is a good next step after a repair?
options: Verify the original symptom and related operation safely
Assume a new part guarantees success
questions.explanation: Verification confirms whether the repair actually addressed the fault.

questions.question: What should you do before working under a raised vehicle?
options: Ask a helper to hold it up
Use specified lifting points and rated supports on a stable surface
questions.explanation: A jack alone is not a safe support for working underneath.

title: Tools & Measurements
description: Practice tape readings, unit conversions, threads and choosing the right tool.

lessons.title: Measure before cutting
lessons.body: Check the unit, zero point and scale. Convert fractions carefully and mark your reference edge.

lessons.title: Match tools and fasteners
lessons.body: Socket size is not bolt diameter. Match thread diameter and pitch, and use the appropriate drill-and-tap chart.

questions.question: A tape has 16 equal divisions per inch. What is the fifth division after 2 inches?
questions.explanation: Each division is 1/16 inch, so five divisions add 5/16.

questions.question: What is 3/8 inch as a decimal?
questions.explanation: Three divided by eight equals 0.375.

questions.question: How many millimeters equal exactly one inch?
questions.explanation: The international inch is defined as exactly 25.4 millimeters.

questions.question: What is 2 inches in millimeters?
questions.explanation: Multiply 2 by 25.4 to obtain 50.8 millimeters.

questions.question: What is 1/2 inch plus 1/4 inch?
questions.explanation: One half is two quarters; adding one quarter gives three quarters.

questions.question: What is 7/8 inch minus 1/4 inch?
questions.explanation: Convert one quarter to two eighths, then subtract.

questions.question: What is 0.125 inch as a fraction?
questions.explanation: One divided by eight equals 0.125.

questions.question: Which instrument can measure an outside diameter with jaws?
questions.explanation: A caliper's outside jaws measure external dimensions.

questions.question: What is a feeler gauge commonly used to measure?
questions.explanation: Thin calibrated blades measure gaps between surfaces.

questions.question: What does a torque wrench measure or control?
questions.explanation: Torque is turning force expressed as force multiplied by distance.

questions.question: What unit is commonly used for metric torque?
questions.explanation: Newton-meters express force times lever-arm distance.

questions.question: What does M8 × 1.25 identify?
options: 8 mm length and 1.25 mm head width
8 mm nominal thread diameter and 1.25 mm pitch
8 mm wrench size and 1.25 mm length
8 threads per inch and 1.25 inch diameter
questions.explanation: Metric thread notation specifies nominal diameter and distance between threads.

questions.question: What does TPI mean?
questions.explanation: In inch-thread systems, pitch is often expressed as threads per inch.

questions.question: Which tool identifies thread pitch?
questions.explanation: The gauge's teeth are compared with the fastener threads.

questions.question: Why is a tap-drill hole normally smaller than the thread's nominal diameter?
options: Material must remain for the internal thread
The bolt head must fit inside
questions.explanation: A tap cuts or forms threads in the remaining hole wall.

questions.question: What should determine tap-drill selection?
options: A guess based on bolt length
Thread specification and an appropriate chart
questions.explanation: Thread size, pitch and tap type determine suitable drill selection.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of a center punch before drilling?
questions.explanation: A suitable punch mark helps locate the drill's starting position.

questions.question: What does a square help check?
questions.explanation: A square compares an edge or joint with a 90-degree reference.

questions.question: What is 150 mm in centimeters?
questions.explanation: Ten millimeters equal one centimeter.

questions.question: What should you do before trusting a precision measurement?
questions.explanation: A dirty surface or incorrect zero can produce misleading readings.

title: Boating Safety
description: Learn basic navigation awareness, trip preparation and onboard safety.

lessons.title: Prepare before departure
lessons.body: Check weather, equipment, fuel and your boat. Share a float plan and ensure life jackets fit the people using them.

lessons.title: Understand local waters
lessons.body: Navigation rules and aids depend on location and circumstances. Study official rules and complete required instruction; this quiz does not issue a boating certificate.

questions.question: Which side is port when facing the bow?
questions.explanation: Port is the vessel's left side when facing forward.

questions.question: Which side is starboard when facing the bow?
questions.explanation: Starboard is the vessel's right side when facing forward.

questions.question: What color is a vessel's port sidelight?
questions.explanation: The port sidelight is red under navigation rules.

questions.question: What color is a vessel's starboard sidelight?
questions.explanation: The starboard sidelight is green under navigation rules.

questions.question: What is the bow?
questions.explanation: The bow is the forward end.

questions.question: What is the stern?
questions.explanation: The stern is the aft end.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a float plan?
options: Tell a trusted person your trip details and expected return
questions.explanation: A float plan helps others raise the alarm if you fail to return.

questions.question: When is the best time to put on a properly fitted life jacket?
questions.explanation: Wearing it beforehand provides protection when an emergency occurs suddenly.

questions.question: What is a key life-jacket selection factor?
options: Fit and intended use for the wearer
questions.explanation: An unsuitable or poorly fitted jacket may not perform as intended.

questions.question: What should you check before leaving the dock?
options: Weather, boat condition and required safety equipment
questions.explanation: A pre-departure check reduces preventable problems.

questions.question: What should a boat operator maintain while underway?
options: A fixed course regardless of traffic
questions.explanation: Lookout includes observing traffic, hazards and changing conditions.

questions.question: What does safe speed depend on?
options: Visibility, traffic, conditions and maneuvering ability
questions.explanation: Safe speed must permit appropriate action for the actual situation.

questions.question: For two power-driven vessels meeting head-on with risk of collision, what is the usual rule?
questions.explanation: The head-on rule generally calls for starboard alterations so vessels pass port to port.

questions.question: When you overtake another vessel, what is your responsibility?
options: Force it to move out of your way
Keep clear of the vessel being overtaken
questions.explanation: An overtaking vessel must keep clear until finally past and clear.

questions.question: Does being the stand-on vessel permit ignoring a collision threat?
options: Yes, if your vessel is larger
Yes, if you sounded the horn
Yes, holding course always takes priority
questions.explanation: All operators must act as required to avoid collision.

questions.question: What is carbon monoxide?
questions.explanation: Engine exhaust can contain dangerous CO without a detectable smell.

questions.question: Where can engine exhaust create a CO hazard?
options: Only inside a closed fuel tank
Only below the engine's oil level
questions.explanation: CO can accumulate in occupied areas or near exhaust outlets.

questions.question: What should happen before approaching a swimmer with a propeller-driven boat?
options: Increase RPM to improve steering beside the swimmer
Let the swimmer hold the propeller
Keep clear and stop propulsion before the person approaches the propeller area
questions.explanation: A rotating propeller is a serious injury hazard; maintain separation and shut down appropriately.

questions.question: What is an engine cut-off lanyard intended to do?
options: Stop the engine if the operator is separated from the controls
questions.explanation: Use the cut-off system as directed for the vessel and situation.

questions.question: What should you do if you do not understand a waterway marker?
options: Follow the nearest boat without checking
Slow safely and consult the chart and official local guidance
Assume all markers mean safe water
Use the color as a speed limit
questions.explanation: Marker systems and meanings require proper interpretation.

title: Trailer & Towing Basics
description: Practice hitch checks, load ratings, tire checks and safe trip planning.

lessons.title: Check the complete combination
lessons.body: Use the tow vehicle and trailer manuals. Check all ratings, coupling compatibility, lights, brakes, safety connections and tires.

lessons.title: Plan for the load
lessons.body: Secure cargo and account for tongue load, payload and actual loaded weight. Allow more space and use qualified instruction before towing on busy roads.

questions.question: Which rating limits the loaded weight of the trailer itself?
questions.explanation: GVWR is the maximum specified loaded weight of that vehicle or trailer.

questions.question: Which rating concerns the loaded tow vehicle and trailer together?
questions.explanation: GCWR is the manufacturer's gross combination weight rating.

questions.question: Does hitch capacity alone establish a vehicle's safe towing capacity?
options: Yes, if the ball is new
No, all applicable vehicle and component limits matter
questions.explanation: The complete combination must remain within every applicable rating.

questions.question: What does trailer tongue load contribute to on the tow vehicle?
questions.explanation: Tongue load is carried by the tow vehicle and consumes available capacity.

questions.question: How should you choose the hitch-ball diameter?
questions.explanation: The coupler and ball must have the specified compatible dimensions.

questions.question: What should you verify after closing the trailer coupler?
options: Only that the jack is down
Only that the latch can move freely
It is fully seated, locked and secured as specified
questions.explanation: An incompletely coupled trailer can separate from the tow vehicle.

questions.question: Why use required safety chains or cables?
options: Eliminate the need for trailer brakes
Provide a secondary connection if the hitch separates
questions.explanation: Safety connections supplement the hitch rather than replace it.

questions.question: What should you check about safety-chain length and routing?
options: Enough turning clearance without dragging, following the manual
They drag to mark the road
They are tied to the brake hose
questions.explanation: Correct routing must accommodate normal movement without creating hazards.

questions.question: What is a breakaway brake system intended to do?
options: Apply trailer brakes if the trailer separates
questions.explanation: Where fitted, the system uses a separation trigger to apply trailer braking.

questions.question: What should you do with the trailer jack before travel?
options: Remove the safety chains to clear it
Use it as a wheel chock
Raise and secure it as specified
questions.explanation: A deployed jack can strike the road or obstacles.

questions.question: What is the best way to confirm trailer lights work?
options: Assume the tow vehicle lights prove it
Test each required function before departure
questions.explanation: Connections or lamps can fail even if the vehicle lights work.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a trailer brake controller where required?
questions.explanation: A controller operates compatible electric trailer brakes according to its setup.

questions.question: How should cargo be secured?
options: With suitable rated restraints and correct anchor points
By relying only on its weight
By placing a tarp without restraints
questions.explanation: Cargo can move during braking, turning and road vibration.

questions.question: When should restraints and connections be rechecked?
options: At safe stops and as the manuals recommend
questions.explanation: Loads can settle and connections can loosen during travel.

questions.question: Why allow extra following distance when towing?
options: The combination needs more room to react and stop
questions.explanation: Additional weight and length change stopping and maneuvering needs.

questions.question: Why do trailer wheels often need extra clearance in a turn?
options: They automatically match the front wheels
They may track inside the tow vehicle's path
They always track outside every curve
questions.explanation: Off-tracking can bring trailer wheels close to curbs or obstacles.

questions.question: Why practice backing in a clear area first?
options: Trailer response differs from the tow vehicle's response
It changes the trailer's weight rating
It removes the need for mirrors
questions.explanation: Backing a trailer requires learned steering and observation skills.

questions.question: What should you inspect on trailer tires?
options: Only the tread's appearance from afar
questions.explanation: Use the specified pressure and rating; inspect for damage and deterioration.

questions.question: Why use wheel chocks when preparing to unhitch on a suitable surface?
questions.explanation: Chocks resist rolling while the trailer is being secured and supported.

questions.question: What is the best way to know actual loaded trailer weight?
questions.explanation: Scale measurements help compare the loaded combination with its ratings.

title: Small-Engine Basics
description: Understand lawn equipment, generators, fuel, ignition and routine maintenance.

lessons.title: Identify the engine
lessons.body: Use the engine model and equipment manual to select fuel, oil, filters and spark plugs. Two-stroke and four-stroke lubrication arrangements can differ.

lessons.title: Prevent accidental starting
lessons.body: Stop the engine, let hot parts cool and isolate ignition and other energy sources as the manual directs before service. Operate combustion engines outdoors.

questions.question: What should identify the correct maintenance parts for a small engine?
options: Any part with a similar picture
questions.explanation: Model-specific information helps select compatible service parts.

questions.question: What does the air filter protect against?
questions.explanation: The filter limits abrasive dirt in intake air.

questions.question: Should every foam and paper air filter be serviced the same way?
options: Yes, wash every filter with gasoline
Yes, soak every filter in oil
questions.explanation: Filter construction determines the correct cleaning or replacement method.

questions.question: What does a carburetor do?
options: Mix fuel and air for combustion
questions.explanation: A carburetor meters fuel into incoming air.

questions.question: What does a choke normally do for cold starting?
options: Enrich the mixture by restricting intake air
questions.explanation: A choke restricts air to provide a richer starting mixture.

questions.question: What should normally happen to a manual choke as the engine warms?
options: Use it to regulate tire pressure
Move toward the normal running position as instructed
questions.explanation: Warm-running operation usually needs less enrichment.

questions.question: What is the main function of a spark plug in a gasoline small engine?
questions.explanation: The plug provides the spark that ignites the mixture.

questions.question: How should you determine spark-plug gap?
options: Use the engine specification and correct measuring tool
Use one universal gap for every engine
Guess from the old plug's color
questions.explanation: Plug type and gap are engine-specific.

questions.question: What can degraded fuel cause?
questions.explanation: Fuel quality can deteriorate during storage.

questions.question: What should guide fuel-stabilizer use?
options: Use it instead of engine oil
Product directions and the engine's storage guidance
questions.explanation: Use only suitable products at the specified concentration.

questions.question: What does a governor generally regulate?
options: Engine operating speed under changing load
questions.explanation: A governor adjusts engine output to maintain the intended speed.

questions.question: What should you do with a governor if the engine seems slow?
options: Diagnose using the manual rather than bypassing it
questions.explanation: Overspeed can damage equipment and create hazards.

questions.question: What is the crankcase oil's role in a typical four-stroke engine?
questions.explanation: Use the specified oil and maintain the correct level.

questions.question: Where do many premix two-stroke engines get lubrication?
options: Oil mixed with fuel at the specified ratio
questions.explanation: Premix engines require the specified oil-fuel ratio; other designs may use injection.

questions.question: What should you do if you are unsure whether an engine requires premix?
options: Add an arbitrary amount of oil
Choose based on exhaust color alone
Assume all engines use plain gasoline
questions.explanation: Incorrect fuel or lubrication can damage the engine.

questions.question: What do cooling fins help do on an air-cooled engine?
options: Transfer engine heat to the air
questions.explanation: Clean fins and correct airflow help cooling.

questions.question: What should happen before working near a mower blade?
options: Stop and isolate the equipment as directed
Rely only on the throttle being low
Ask someone to hold the blade
questions.explanation: Prevent accidental starting and movement before service.

questions.question: When should a gasoline-powered engine be refueled?
options: After shutdown and cooling as specified, away from ignition sources
questions.explanation: Fuel vapors and hot surfaces create a fire hazard.

questions.question: Where should a portable combustion generator run?
options: Inside a basement near a fan
Outdoors away from building openings according to safety guidance
Inside a garage with one window open
questions.explanation: Generator exhaust can produce lethal carbon monoxide.

questions.question: What should you do before restarting equipment after service?
options: Start it at maximum speed immediately
Check correct reassembly, guards and safe operation
Remove guards to watch moving parts
questions.explanation: Inspection and safe verification help catch assembly errors.

title: Welding Fundamentals
description: Learn welding terminology, joint types and hazard awareness.

lessons.title: Learn the process
lessons.body: Understand the material, joint and welding process before selecting settings. Obtain supervised training before practical work.

lessons.title: Control the hazards
lessons.body: Address fire, fumes, electrical hazards and eye exposure. Protective equipment does not replace ventilation, safe setup or appropriate training.

questions.question: What is a weld joint?
options: The arrangement where parts are joined by welding
questions.explanation: Joint configuration determines how parts meet and are joined.

questions.question: What is a butt joint?
options: A rod inside a closed tank
A cable wrapped around a pipe
Two parts meeting edge to edge
questions.explanation: Butt joints join adjoining edges.

questions.question: What is a lap joint?
options: Two parts meeting only at their ends
questions.explanation: Overlap distinguishes a lap joint.

questions.question: What is a T-joint?
options: One part meeting another in a T arrangement
Two plates joined end to end
questions.explanation: The parts form a T shape before joining.

questions.question: What is filler metal?
options: Material added to form the joint
Oil used to cool the helmet
questions.explanation: Filler can come from a rod, wire or electrode, depending on the process.

questions.question: What is the function of shielding gas in applicable welding processes?
options: Protect the weld area from atmospheric contamination
questions.explanation: Suitable shielding limits atmospheric effects on the molten weld.

questions.question: What does GTAW stand for?
questions.explanation: GTAW uses a tungsten electrode and is commonly called TIG.

questions.question: What does GMAW stand for?
questions.explanation: GMAW uses a continuously fed consumable wire electrode.

questions.question: What does SMAW stand for?
questions.explanation: SMAW is commonly called stick welding.

questions.question: What is a tack weld used for?
options: Hold parts in position before completing the joint
questions.explanation: Tacks help maintain fit-up, but the final procedure still matters.

questions.question: What is weld penetration?
options: Depth of fusion into the base material
questions.explanation: Penetration concerns fusion within the joint.

questions.question: What is weld porosity?
questions.explanation: Trapped gas can leave cavities that affect weld quality.

questions.question: What is slag in processes that produce it?
options: A nonmetallic layer formed from flux
questions.explanation: Slag may need removal between passes according to the procedure.

questions.question: Why clean and identify coatings before welding?
options: Coatings eliminate the need for ventilation
Coatings can affect weld quality and create hazardous fumes
questions.explanation: Material preparation must account for both quality and exposure hazards.

questions.question: Why protect nearby people from an arc?
options: Arc radiation can injure exposed eyes and skin
Arc light makes batteries lose charge
questions.explanation: Use suitable screens and other controls for bystanders.

questions.question: What should determine welding lens shade and protective equipment?
options: The process, exposure and applicable guidance
questions.explanation: Protection must suit the actual welding conditions.

questions.question: Is a welding helmet alone enough to control welding fumes?
options: No, appropriate fume controls are also needed
Yes, if the visor is dark
questions.explanation: Eye protection does not provide ventilation or respiratory protection.

questions.question: What should you do before hot work near combustible material?
options: Remove or protect combustibles and follow the hot-work procedure
questions.explanation: Fire prevention must be planned before welding or cutting.

questions.question: What should a beginner do with a used fuel tank needing welding?
options: Assume an empty tank cannot explode
Test it with an open flame
Refer it to qualified specialists using approved procedures
Weld it after a quick rinse
questions.explanation: Residual vapors can explode; do not treat empty containers as safe.

questions.question: Why obtain qualified inspection for a safety-critical weld?
options: Appearance alone cannot prove the joint is suitable
A smooth bead always proves full strength
questions.explanation: Required inspection and acceptance criteria depend on the application.

title: Electrical & Diagnostic Basics
description: Practice units, circuits and safe low-voltage diagnostic principles.

lessons.title: Understand the circuit
lessons.body: Trace power, protection, loads and return paths. Compare measurements with a wiring diagram and specifications.

lessons.title: Use the correct meter setup
lessons.body: Inspect leads and select the appropriate function and jacks. Resistance checks require a safely de-energized circuit. This section is introductory, not instruction to work on mains or EV high-voltage systems.

questions.question: Which unit measures voltage?
questions.explanation: Voltage is electrical potential difference, measured in volts.

questions.question: Which unit measures current?
questions.explanation: Current is charge flow, measured in amperes.

questions.question: Which unit measures resistance?
questions.explanation: Resistance opposes current and is measured in ohms.

questions.question: Which unit measures electrical power?
questions.explanation: Power is the rate of energy transfer.

questions.question: What is Ohm's law for a simple resistor?
questions.explanation: Voltage equals current multiplied by resistance.

questions.question: A 6-ohm resistor has 12 volts across it. What current flows?
questions.explanation: Using I = V/R gives 12/6 = 2 amperes.

questions.question: A load draws 3 A at 12 V. What is its electrical power?
questions.explanation: Power equals voltage multiplied by current: 12 × 3 = 36 watts.

questions.question: What is an open circuit?
options: A complete path with no interruption
questions.explanation: A broken path prevents intended current flow through it.

questions.question: What is a short circuit?
options: A cable cut to its ideal length
questions.explanation: A short can allow excessive current through an unintended path.

questions.question: What does a correctly rated fuse primarily protect against?
questions.explanation: A fuse interrupts excessive current under its specified operating conditions.

questions.question: What should replace a blown fuse after diagnosing the fault?
options: The specified fuse type and rating
A higher rating to prevent blowing
questions.explanation: Increasing the rating or bypassing protection can create a fire hazard.

questions.question: How is voltage normally measured across a component?
options: With the circuit's fuse removed permanently
With the meter connected in parallel
By replacing the component with the meter's current input
Only by measuring its physical length
questions.explanation: Voltage is measured between two points.

questions.question: What should happen before a resistance measurement?
options: Safely remove power and address stored energy
Switch the meter to its current jack
questions.explanation: Resistance testing uses the meter's source and requires a de-energized circuit.

questions.question: What does a continuity test generally check?
options: Whether a device can carry full operating load
Whether a battery has its original capacity
Whether a wire has the correct color
questions.explanation: Continuity does not by itself prove a connection performs well under load.

questions.question: Why test voltage drop under load?
options: A weak connection may appear acceptable without current flow
questions.explanation: Resistance in a connection produces a voltage drop as current flows.

questions.question: What is a relay?
questions.explanation: A relay allows one circuit to control switching in another.

questions.question: What does DC mean?
questions.explanation: DC describes current with a consistent direction.

questions.question: What does AC mean?
questions.explanation: AC changes direction periodically.

questions.question: What should you do with a damaged test lead?
options: Stop using it and replace it appropriately
Wrap bare wire around the probe
questions.explanation: Damaged insulation or connections can create shock and measurement hazards.

questions.question: What is the best first step when unfamiliar with an EV high-voltage system?
options: Seek qualified training and follow manufacturer safety procedures
Assume disconnecting the 12-volt battery makes it safe
questions.explanation: High-voltage systems require specialized procedures and qualification.

title: Workshop Safety
description: Recognize common hazards around tools, lifting, machinery and stored energy.

lessons.title: Plan the job
lessons.body: Identify hazards, choose suitable tools and protective equipment, and keep the work area organized. Training and manufacturer instructions come first.

lessons.title: Control all energy
lessons.body: Shutdown alone may not isolate electricity, pressure, springs or gravity. Follow the applicable energy-control procedure before maintenance.

questions.question: What should you do with a damaged hand tool?
options: Remove it from use until properly repaired or replaced
Use it only on harder jobs
questions.explanation: Damaged tools can fail or slip unexpectedly.

questions.question: What should guide tool selection?
options: The task and tool manufacturer's instructions
questions.explanation: Use tools suitable for the material and operation.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a machine guard?
options: Limit access to hazardous moving parts
questions.explanation: Guards reduce exposure to moving components and other hazards.

questions.question: What should you do if a guard interferes with the job?
options: Stop and use an approved setup or procedure
questions.explanation: Do not bypass protective equipment to complete a task.

questions.question: Why secure a workpiece before drilling?
options: Prevent unexpected movement and improve control
Remove every need for eye protection
questions.explanation: An unsecured workpiece can rotate or shift.

questions.question: What is the best practice around rotating machinery?
options: Use loose gloves near every rotating part
Secure loose clothing, hair and jewelry
questions.explanation: Entanglement hazards require clothing and PPE choices suited to the equipment.

questions.question: What should you do before changing a power-tool accessory?
options: Leave it plugged in and cover the switch
Ask a helper to slow the spindle
Isolate power as directed by the manufacturer
questions.explanation: Accidental starting during accessory changes can cause injury.

questions.question: Why inspect a power cord before use?
options: A long cord always carries more current safely
questions.explanation: Check insulation, plugs and connections before use.

questions.question: What should you do when a tool starts vibrating abnormally?
questions.explanation: Abnormal vibration may indicate damage or incorrect setup.

questions.question: What does a safety data sheet provide?
options: Information about a chemical's hazards and precautions
questions.explanation: SDS information supports safe handling and exposure controls.

questions.question: Why label chemical containers appropriately?
options: Make incompatible chemicals safe to mix
questions.explanation: Clear identification helps avoid accidental misuse.

questions.question: What should you do with an unexpected spill?
options: Ignore it until the next shift
Isolate the hazard and follow the appropriate cleanup procedure
Wash every spill into a storm drain
questions.explanation: The material and circumstances determine safe cleanup.

questions.question: What is a pinch point?
options: An area where body parts can be caught between moving or closing objects
questions.explanation: Crushing and trapping hazards occur where movement closes a gap.

questions.question: What is stored energy?
options: Only current flowing in a live cord
Only a running engine's fuel use
Energy remaining in systems such as springs, pressure or raised loads
questions.explanation: A stopped machine can still contain hazardous energy.

questions.question: Does pressing a stop button necessarily isolate all hazardous energy?
options: Yes, if the lamp turns off
Yes, if the machine is quiet
No, isolation and verification may still be required
Yes, it always disconnects every source
questions.explanation: Control switches do not necessarily isolate the energy source.

questions.question: Who should carry out workplace lockout procedures?
options: Trained authorized personnel under the applicable procedure
Anyone who finds a spare padlock
questions.explanation: Energy control requires appropriate authorization, training and procedures.

questions.question: Why use rated lifting equipment?
options: Loads must remain within equipment capacity
A larger hook makes ratings irrelevant
questions.explanation: Capacity and correct use matter for every lift.

questions.question: What should you do when a suspended load is overhead?
options: Stand under it to guide it
Hold it up with a broom
Keep clear of the load and its potential fall path
questions.explanation: A suspended load can fall or move unexpectedly.

questions.question: Why keep exits and walkways clear?
options: Permit safe movement and emergency escape
questions.explanation: Obstructions create trip hazards and delay evacuation.

questions.question: When should you stop a job and ask for help?
options: Never if the deadline is close
When the procedure, equipment or hazard is beyond your training
questions.explanation: Recognizing your limits is part of safe work.

title: Parts & Project Planning
description: Practice fitment checks, inspection, budgeting and responsible buying or selling.

lessons.title: Confirm compatibility
lessons.body: Match model, year, application, part numbers and relevant dimensions. Ask for clear photos and verify important details with manufacturer information.

lessons.title: Plan the complete repair
lessons.body: Include related parts, fluids, tools and verification in your budget. Describe used parts honestly and protect private information in listings.

questions.question: What is the strongest fitment check before buying a replacement part?
options: Verified application data and compatible part specifications
questions.explanation: Confirm the intended application and specifications rather than appearance alone.

questions.question: Why ask for a part number?
options: It proves the part is undamaged
It helps identify the component and verify cross-references
questions.explanation: Part numbers help identification but do not establish condition.

questions.question: What should you do when a listing's compatibility is unclear?
options: Modify safety-critical parts to force a fit
Ask for details and verify before buying
questions.explanation: Clarification reduces the risk of buying an unsuitable part.

questions.question: What is useful in photos of a used part?
options: Multiple clear views of markings and condition
Only a distant photo of the box
Only a stock photo with no condition details
questions.explanation: Actual detailed photos help buyers assess the item.

questions.question: How should a seller describe a known defect?
options: Clearly disclose it in the listing
questions.explanation: Honest condition descriptions help buyers make informed decisions.

questions.question: What does untested mean in a used-parts listing?
questions.explanation: Untested status should not be treated as a performance guarantee.

questions.question: Why keep dimensions and units together?
questions.explanation: A number without a unit can lead to a wrong selection.

questions.question: What should a repair budget include besides the main part?
options: Related supplies, tools and possible labor
questions.explanation: The full project may require seals, fluids, fasteners or professional work.

questions.question: Why identify the fault before ordering parts?
options: Ensure every job uses more parts
Guarantee the first guess is right
questions.explanation: Diagnosis helps select a repair based on the actual cause.

questions.question: How should you compare two suppliers' prices?
options: Assume the cheapest photo is identical
Compare compatible items and total cost with stated terms
questions.explanation: Fitment, quantity, condition, shipping and terms affect the comparison.

questions.question: What should you check before relying on a return option?
options: Assume all used parts can be returned
questions.explanation: Return conditions differ and should be understood before purchase.

questions.question: What is important when packing a sharp or heavy part?
options: Suitable padding, containment and a strong package
questions.explanation: Packaging should prevent movement, punctures and handling damage.

questions.question: What should you do before shipping a battery or fluid-containing component?
options: Check carrier restrictions and safe packaging requirements
questions.explanation: Some items require special handling or may be restricted.

questions.question: Which information should you avoid exposing in a public listing?
questions.explanation: Keep financial and identity information private.

questions.question: What is a warning sign during an online transaction?
options: A request for another part photo
Pressure to share verification codes or pay by an unusual method
questions.explanation: Verification codes and payment pressure can be scam indicators.

questions.question: Where is a sensible place to arrange a local exchange?
options: A suitable public location with a safety plan
An isolated location demanded at the last moment
A place where you cannot contact anyone
questions.explanation: Choose arrangements that support personal safety and inspection.

questions.question: What should you confirm before buying safety-critical used components?
options: Suitability and condition through appropriate qualified assessment
That the seller used the word racing
That they are cheaper than new
questions.explanation: Some components are unsuitable for reuse; expert assessment may be necessary.

questions.question: Why label removed parts and fasteners during disassembly?
options: Guarantee every part can be reused
Help track locations and reassembly requirements
questions.explanation: Labels and notes reduce assembly errors.

questions.question: What should happen after a project is complete?
options: Skip inspection if it looks clean
Verify function safely and record relevant work
questions.explanation: Safe verification checks whether the intended result was achieved.

questions.question: What should you do when a part cannot be safely reused?
options: Follow suitable recycling or disposal guidance
questions.explanation: Responsible disposal and honest descriptions protect others and the environment.

title: Hydrogen Vehicles & Fuel Cells
description: Learn hydrogen vehicle theory, fuel-cell operation, energy flow, production and safety awareness. This module explains principles; it does not teach high-pressure or high-voltage repair.

lessons.title: Two ways to use hydrogen
lessons.body: A fuel-cell electric vehicle (FCEV) makes electricity onboard and drives its wheels with a motor. A hydrogen combustion engine burns fuel to move pistons. These are different systems. Burning hydrogen in air can create nitrogen oxides; a pure-hydrogen fuel cell does not use combustion.

lessons.title: Inside a PEM fuel cell
lessons.body: PEM means proton exchange membrane. Hydrogen enters one side and oxygen arrives in air on the other. At the catalyst, hydrogen separates into protons and electrons. Protons cross the membrane while electrons travel through an outside circuit, supplying current. Their reaction with oxygen forms water and releases heat. Multiple cells form a stack.

lessons.title: Follow the energy
lessons.body: Stored hydrogen supplies the stack; electrical power reaches the traction motor through power electronics. A traction battery buffers energy and captures some braking energy. The motor turns the wheels through the drivetrain. Cooling controls component temperatures. A DC/DC converter supplies lower-voltage accessories. Exact layouts vary by vehicle.

lessons.title: Where the fuel comes from
lessons.body: Hydrogen carries energy; producing it also takes energy. Electrolysis uses electricity to separate water into hydrogen and oxygen. Other processes obtain hydrogen from fuels such as natural gas. Production, electricity supply and delivery affect the overall environmental result. Water at the vehicle exhaust does not mean the entire supply chain has no emissions.

lessons.title: Safety awareness, not a repair procedure
lessons.body: Vehicle hydrogen storage uses specialized equipment. Hydrogen can ignite readily and its flame can be difficult to see. Ventilation and engineered detection matter. High-voltage components also require trained service. Do not open tanks, loosen hydrogen fittings, bypass protective controls or attempt energized electrical work. For a suspected leak or damaged vehicle, keep away and contact emergency responders or qualified service as appropriate.

lessons.title: Study with reliable information
lessons.body: Use this module to learn the principles and vocabulary. Refueling and service instructions must come from the vehicle manufacturer and station operator. Check current station access before planning a journey. APG wrote these lessons and practice questions for independent learning; they are not manufacturer training, certification or an official exam. References below support the technical facts and provide further reading.

sources.label: DOE / AFDC: Hydrogen production and delivery
DOE: Hydrogen combustion and nitrogen oxides

questions.question: What turns the wheels in a fuel-cell electric vehicle?
options: A steam turbine in every model
questions.explanation: The stack supplies electrical energy; a traction motor produces wheel-driving torque.

questions.question: Why can an FCEV also have a traction battery?
options: To buffer power and store recovered braking energy
To manufacture hydrogen from road water
questions.explanation: The battery supports changing power demand and stores energy recovered during braking.

questions.question: Which component supplies lower-voltage accessories from a higher-voltage DC system?
questions.explanation: A DC/DC converter changes the DC voltage level for lower-voltage loads.

questions.question: Why does a fuel-cell vehicle need cooling?
options: Hydrogen must burn inside the radiator
Its stack and electrical components produce heat
questions.explanation: Thermal management helps components remain within their operating temperature range.

questions.question: A diagram shows tank, stack, electronics and motor. Which energy sequence is correct?
options: Hydrogen energy, electrical energy, mechanical motion
Hydrogen energy directly rotating the axle
questions.explanation: The stack converts fuel energy into electricity; the motor converts electrical input into motion.

questions.question: In a PEM fuel cell, which particles cross the membrane?
options: Electrons through the intended external circuit
questions.explanation: The membrane conducts protons; electrons take the external electrical path.

questions.question: What makes the external circuit useful in a PEM cell?
options: It removes the need for oxygen
It mechanically turns the fuel tank
Electrons flowing through it provide electrical current
questions.explanation: Separating the proton and electron paths makes electrical current available to a load.

questions.question: Why combine individual fuel cells into a stack?
options: To turn them into combustion cylinders
To obtain a useful combined electrical output
To store gasoline between the cells
questions.explanation: A stack combines the output of multiple electrochemical cells.

questions.question: Which inputs participate in a hydrogen fuel-cell reaction?
questions.explanation: The reaction uses hydrogen with oxygen and produces water and heat while delivering electricity.

questions.question: What does electrolysis use to separate water into hydrogen and oxygen?
questions.explanation: Electrolysis requires electricity; water is a feedstock, not a source of unlimited energy.

questions.question: Is hydrogen necessarily produced from water?
options: Yes; all hydrogen comes from vehicle exhaust
Yes; natural gas cannot be a feedstock
questions.explanation: Hydrogen can be obtained through water electrolysis and processes using other feedstocks.

questions.question: Why does electricity sourcing matter for electrolytic hydrogen?
options: It makes all production emissions identical
It affects the emissions associated with fuel production
questions.explanation: The upstream environmental result depends in part on how the electricity is generated.

questions.question: A claim says water exhaust proves zero emissions everywhere. What is missing?
questions.explanation: Vehicle exhaust is only one part of a supply-chain emissions assessment.

questions.question: What is produced at the exhaust by a vehicle using pure hydrogen in a fuel cell?
options: Diesel particulate matter from the membrane
questions.explanation: A pure-hydrogen fuel cell has no fuel-combustion tailpipe pollutants; upstream impacts still matter.

questions.question: How is a hydrogen combustion engine different from an FCEV?
options: Both must use the same electrochemical stack
It stores hydrogen only as electricity
It burns hydrogen to drive an engine instead of using a fuel cell to supply a motor
questions.explanation: Hydrogen can fuel combustion or electrochemical conversion; the propulsion processes differ.

questions.question: Why can burning hydrogen in air still create nitrogen oxides?
options: High combustion temperatures allow reactions involving nitrogen and oxygen in air
questions.explanation: Hot combustion in air can form NOx even when the fuel contains no carbon.

questions.question: Why are ventilation and leak detection important around hydrogen systems?
options: They guarantee a system can never leak
They help prevent hazardous fuel accumulation and identify releases
They remove the need for trained service
They allow protective controls to be bypassed
questions.explanation: Hydrogen ignition properties call for engineered controls, including detection and ventilation.

questions.question: Why is looking for a visible flame an unreliable hydrogen-fire check?
options: A hydrogen flame can be very difficult to see
All hydrogen fires produce thick black smoke
A flame is visible only through a vehicle dashboard
questions.explanation: Special detection may be needed; do not approach a suspected fire to inspect it.

questions.question: What should an untrained person do after suspecting a hydrogen-system leak?
options: Loosen a fitting to release pressure
Disable the leak warning and keep driving
Use a flame to locate the leak
Keep away and seek appropriate emergency or qualified assistance
questions.explanation: Do not attempt leak testing or repairs. Keep clear and obtain appropriate help.

questions.question: Does passing this practice quiz qualify someone to service an FCEV?
options: Yes; it replaces all electrical training
No; hands-on work requires suitable training and manufacturer procedures
questions.explanation: APG practice is a learning aid, not a service credential or permission for hazardous work.
